finding_01_volume_reduction.title: Sustained Reduction in Total Collision Volume Post-2020
finding_01_volume_reduction.claim: Monthly reported collisions plummeted by 77.9% during the April 2020 COVID-19 lockdown and have settled at ~8,132 crashes/month post-2021, compared to a pre-COVID baseline of 18,693 crashes/month (2015-2019).

finding_02_injury_rate_paradox.title: The Severity Inversion: Sharply Higher Proportion of Injury Collisions Post-COVID
finding_02_injury_rate_paradox.claim: While total collision volume decreased, the proportion of collisions resulting in injury or death increased dramatically from 19.3% pre-COVID (2013-2019 average) to 40.0% post-COVID (2021-2025 average), a +20.8 percentage point increase.

finding_03_temporal_rhythms.title: Bimodal Diurnal Traffic Commuter Peaks and High-Risk Weekend Early Hours
finding_03_temporal_rhythms.claim: Reported collisions peak sharply on Friday between 16:00 and 17:00 (26,107 cumulative collisions), driven by evening commuter congestion. In contrast, late-night and weekend early AM hours (02:00-05:00) feature the lowest total crash volume but elevated severe/fatal outcomes associated with alcohol and speeding.

finding_04_spatial_concentration.title: High Crash Density Corridors Concentrated along Major Arterials and Expressways
finding_04_spatial_concentration.claim: Geographic collision density is heavily clustered around high-volume interchange corridors: Midtown Manhattan (42nd St & FDR Drive), Downtown Brooklyn (Flatbush & Atlantic Ave), Queens Blvd / Long Island Expressway, and Cross Bronx Expressway.

finding_05_vru_disproportionate_lethalit.title: Extreme Vulnerability of Pedestrians and Cyclists to Fatal Outcomes
finding_05_vru_disproportionate_lethalit.claim: While motor vehicle occupants account for the majority of injured victims (540,227 injured, 1,466 killed; fatality rate of 2.71 deaths per 1,000 injured), pedestrians suffer a fatality rate of 13.10 deaths per 1,000 injured (4.83x higher than motorists) and represent more total fatalities (1,805) than vehicle occupants.

finding_06_speeding_lethality.title: Unsafe Speeding and Traffic Disregard Exhibit Disproportionate Lethality
finding_06_speeding_lethality.claim: Driver Inattention is the most frequent contributing factor (484,012 crashes; 10.29 fatalities per 10k crashes). However, Unsafe Speeding exhibits an extreme fatality rate of 131.04 deaths per 10,000 crashes (12.7x higher than inattention) with a 43.2% injury rate.

finding_07_data_governance_gap.title: Significant Administrative Geocoding Gaps: Missing Borough vs Valid Coordinates
finding_07_data_governance_gap.claim: 30.5% (691,375 records) lack an administrative Borough string. However, 488,444 of these records possess valid, high-precision GPS coordinates within NYC municipal limits. Conducting borough-level comparisons based solely on raw text strings discards over 21.5% of spatial data.
